narrative:
On July 27, 2026, the Karnataka High Court achieved an overall hearing rate of 44.7%, taking up 1,329 out of 2,972 scheduled cases across 42 judges. This reflects an operational improvement compared to prior court days, rising from 36.9% on July 24 and 42.0% on July 23, even while managing a significantly higher total caseload.

High-volume output was led by Justice S Vishwajith Shetty, who heard 131 out of 298 scheduled cases, and Justice M. Nagaprasanna, who processed 196 total cases across two listings. Notable individual efficiency highlights included Justice Pradeep Singh Yerur with a 75.0% hearing rate (42 heard out of 56), Justice Shivashankar Amarannavar at 73.4% (58 heard out of 79), and Justice V Srishananda at 73.0% (73 heard out of 100). Conversely, certain listings experienced minimal movement, including Justice Ravi V Hosmani with 0 out of 60 cases heard and a major listing under Justice B M Shyam Prasad converting only 7 out of 129 scheduled cases (5.4%).

Stage-wise analysis reveals higher conversion rates in early procedural stages, with Preliminary Hearings reaching 57.6% (217 of 377) and Orders converting 49.7% (451 of 908). However, Final Hearings continued to lag with a conversion rate of 20.9% (106 of 506 heard), down from 32.2% on July 24 and 24.4% on July 23. In terms of case type distribution, Writ Petitions (WP) formed the largest segment with 1,271 scheduled and 546 heard (43.0%, improving from 35.6% on July 24). Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) registered a significant clearance increase to 45.2% (239 heard) compared to 25.6% on July 24, while Regular Second Appeals (RSA) delivered a strong conversion rate of 67.8% (82 of 121 heard).
